best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway season of 2020 stands as one of the most abbreviated in theater history, cut short by the pandemic shutdown that would darken marquees for over a year. Yet the handful of productions that managed to open before March 12, 2020, left a significant mark on the theatrical landscape.

Leading our rankings is **Les Misérables**, which earns an 83/100 with its grittier, reimagined production at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This revival strips away some of the original's grand spectacle in favor of a more intimate, visceral approach that resonates with most critics, though purists remain divided.

Close behind is **A Soldier's Play** (78/100), Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that finally received its long-overdue Broadway premiere. The production's examination of race, power, and justice within a segregated World War II Army base proves as urgent and relevant today as when Fuller first wrote it, with critics praising both the stellar ensemble cast and the play's continued resonance.

Rounding out the top five are **Grand Horizons** (73/100), a boulevard comedy elevated by Jane Alexander's performance; **My Name is Lucy Barton** (71/100), featuring Laura Linney's widely praised solo turn in this Elizabeth Strout adaptation; and **West Side Story** (68/100), Ivo van Hove's polarizing reimagining that sparked intense debate about how far one can push a canonical work.

With an average score of 75/100 across these five productions, the abbreviated 2020 season demonstrates both artistic ambition and the enduring power of theatrical storytelling—even in the face of unprecedented disruption.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As we look back from March 2026 at the plays that opened during the 2020 Broadway season—a year dramatically cut short by the pandemic—a small but noteworthy collection of productions managed to make their mark before the shutdown.

Leading the pack is a reimagined **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, where this grittier reboot earns an 83/100 from critics who largely appreciate its fresh approach to the beloved musical, though the production doesn't achieve universal acclaim. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** stands as one of the season's most significant achievements, finally bringing Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama to Broadway in a stellar revival that scores 78/100 across 29 reviews. Critics widely praise the production's powerful examination of race and identity within the military, validating its long-overdue arrival on the Great White Way.

The season's other offerings present a mixed picture. **Grand Horizons** delivers a pleasant if conventional boulevard comedy elevated by veteran performers Jane Alexander and James Cromwell, while **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics despite Laura Linney's universally praised solo performance in this Elizabeth Strout adaptation. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves the season's most polarizing entry, with critics split between those embracing its bold vision and those finding it misguided.

With an average score of 75/100 across these five productions, the brief 2020 season offered quality over quantity, featuring work that ranged from thoughtful revivals to experimental reimaginings. For theatergoers exploring Broadway's recent history, these productions represent a snapshot of a season that promised much before circumstances intervened.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—a year when stages reopened after pandemic shutdowns and artists responded with extraordinary urgency and innovation.

The class of 2021 stands out for its artistic ambition and formal experimentation. Leading the pack is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance to recorded interviews with his mother. Critics consistently describe the production as mesmerizing and unforgettable, awarding it the highest marks of the year. Close behind, **The Lehman Trilogy** earned widespread acclaim as an epic theatrical triumph, with Sam Mendes' stunning direction bringing the 160-year saga of the Lehman Brothers to vivid life across a single evening.

The year also marked Broadway's symbolic reopening with **Pass Over**, Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's urgent drama blending Beckett and Exodus to examine Black American life. Meanwhile, experimental works like **Is This a Room**—a verbatim staging of an FBI transcript—proved that unconventional source material could generate gripping, pulse-pounding theater.

The ten productions featured here average an impressive 81/100 critical score, reflecting both the quality of work presented and perhaps the collective relief and enthusiasm that accompanied theater's return. From Ruben Santiago-Hudson's virtuosic solo turn in **Lackawanna Blues** to Rebecca Frecknall's immersive **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** reimagining, these plays showcase diverse approaches to storytelling while maintaining theatrical excellence.

Whether you're discovering these productions for the first time or revisiting favorites, this guide offers a comprehensive look at the plays that helped Broadway find its voice again.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands as a remarkable period of artistic achievement, marked by an exceptional concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works and inventive revivals that continue to resonate with audiences.

The season's crown jewel is **Kimberly Akimbo**, David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori's quirky musical about a teenager with a rare aging condition. Critics consistently celebrate its masterful balance of comedy and heartbreak, earning it the highest marks of the year. Close behind, **Into the Woods** offers a stripped-down revival that serves as a fitting tribute to the late Stephen Sondheim, with performances that honor the composer's final Broadway season. **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's meta-musical about a Black gay artist, brings brazenly original storytelling that pushes theatrical boundaries while earning both the Pulitzer Prize and widespread critical acclaim.

What distinguishes 2022 is the remarkable presence of multiple Pulitzer-winning plays reaching Broadway stages. Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog**, Tom Stoppard's **Leopoldstadt**, Stephen Adly Guirgis's **Between Riverside and Crazy**, Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive**, and Martyna Majok's **Cost of Living** all demonstrate the season's commitment to substantive, challenging drama. The year also showcases bold new voices like Jordan E. Cooper's provocative satire **Ain't No Mo'** and Mike Birbiglia's intimate solo show exploring mortality.

With an average critical score of 83/100 across these ten productions, the 2022 season represents a high-water mark for contemporary Broadway, offering a diverse range of theatrical experiences that continue to influence the industry today.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:

The production stands alongside other critically acclaimed revivals like **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama that critics have hailed as a modern masterpiece, powered by Sarah Paulson's commanding performance and blistering ensemble work.

The year also marked significant moments for theatrical innovation and representation. **Stranger Things: The First Shadow**, transferring from the West End, proves that properties based on popular media can transcend mere fan service with technically stunning stagecraft. Meanwhile, **Purlie Victorious: A Non-Confederate Romp Through the Cotton Patch** delivers a long-overdue revival of Ossie Davis's 1961 satire, demonstrating how classic works can speak with bracing relevance to contemporary audiences.

From Alex Edelman's solo show **Just for Us** to the Pulitzer Prize-winning **Fat Ham**, from Ben Platt and Micaela Diamond's powerhouse turns in **Parade** to Jodie Comer's tour de force Broadway debut in **Prima Facie**, the class of 2023 represents a remarkable breadth of voices, styles, and perspectives.

Whether you're seeking musical revivals, contemporary dramas, or innovative adaptations, these ten productions offer compelling reasons to experience the vitality of Broadway's dramatic tradition.
